newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate climbs on U.S. rates jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate climbs on U.S. rates jitters.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 105 basis points to 21.25 percent in early trade on fears of U.S. interest rate hikes in the near future in the light of strong U.S. jobs data, dealers and analysts said.

"U.S. rates hikes are very certain now, the unemployment data confirm that, and although rates could remain unchnaged, they are most likely to increase by 25-50 basis points," a trader said, referring to the possible outcome of the July 2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates.
Dealers said Cetes rates had come under additional pressure from a weak peso and pre-weekend demand for liquidity.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 1.6 centavos weaker in early trade at 7.9800/7.9840 per dollar.

Analysts said secondary market rates in Mexico had been under pressure for most of the week as campaigns heated up for the July 6 mid-term elections for Congress, Mexico City mayor and several state governors.

"The market is under pressure. In fact, the last primary auction results showed how investors' outlooks had changed regarding the forthcoming elections. We can see that in overnight rates and leads us to forecast further gains at next week's primary auction," a fixed-income analyst said.
Overnight rates on bank paper mirrored government rates and were up 110 basis points at 22.40 percent.
Liquidity of 1.193 billion pesos was due to return to the system today from prior central bank operations.
